transcript:
[00:00] Priya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we really appreciate the time. quick intro, I'm Priya, AE at Redwood Inference, and I'll be coordinating the onboarding cadence. Marcus and Sofia from CS/SE are with me.
[00:14] Aisha Khan: Hi all, Aisha here — VP Eng at Harborline. we have Tom, Maya and Ben on the line, thanks for setting this up.
[00:22] Tom Reynolds: Hey, Tom — platform lead. we're hoping to get clarity on routing tenants and whether we need dedicated capacity vs hosted in our VPC.
[00:31] Marcus Lee: quick note — we'll take this as the kickoff to map the infra and security needs; also want to surface any blockers early.
[00:38] Sofia Ramos: hi team, I'm Sofia, solutions eng. i'll be running the pilot with you; we'll aim to capture perf, latency, and cost tradeoffs.
[00:45] Ben Park: Ben here, data eng — I'll own the sample prompts and logs for the eval.
[00:51] Maya Singh: Maya, security — i'll need to confirm SOC2 posture and KMS/HSM options.
[00:57] Priya Patel: great. quick agenda — tenant routing model, networking, security, pilot scope, next steps. anything to add?
[01:06] Aisha Khan: maybe timeline — we have a compliance review in early February so it'd be great to have pilot data before then.
[01:12] Priya Patel: noted. let's start with tenant routing. Tom, can you describe your teams and how you'd like requests to be segmented?
[01:20] Tom Reynolds: sure. we have three product teams planning to call the API — patient-intake, care-coordination, and analytics. they'd like logical separation per team, and for analytics we may want higher throughput and private data retention. ideally, we could route by tenant ID and send analytics traffic to dedicated capacity if needed.
[01:39] Sofia Ramos: okay routing by tenant ID is straightforward on our side; the question is whether you want per-tenant dedicated clusters or logical isolation with RBAC and per-tenant model pins. do you have strict data residency or retention differences between teams?
[01:54] Tom Reynolds: patient-intake must avoid logs being retained beyond 30 days and no external export, while analytics can keep longer. we also have PHI concerns for certain endpoints.
[02:05] Maya Singh: yes PHI — we'll need HIPAA considerations documented; also SSO for access to the console and role mapping.
[02:12] Marcus Lee: we have a HIPAA checklist and an encrypted logs retention policy we can share. we'll also surface our Private deployment options if dedicated tenancy is required.
[02:21] Priya Patel: Good. next, networking — Tom, are you running in EKS with private subnets? what does your egress look like?
[02:29] Tom Reynolds: currently EKS in us-west-2, private subnets, NAT for outbound egress. we restrict egress to approved endpoints via proxy; we can't open arbitrary outbound to public APIs.
[02:38] Sofia Ramos: that's common. for Redwood Private we can support VPC peering and private endpoints, or self-hosted on-prem package. if you can't allow outbound to hosted endpoints, we can propose private deployment into your VPC or a colocated PX.
[02:51] Ben Park: if we choose hosted, what's the minimum network changes? we want to avoid big infra reworks.
[02:58] Sofia Ramos: for hosted without peering you'd typically allow a small set of egress IPs and TLS to our API endpoint; for full isolation we recommend VPC peering or Private with our control plane only. we'll send a diagram.
[03:11] Tom Reynolds: ok please send diagram, also need to know load balancer/NAT throughput implications.
[03:16] Priya Patel: noted - action for the SEs to detail peering vs outbound IP approach.
[03:21] Maya Singh: on encryption — we use AWS KMS, we may require customer-managed keys and want confirmation around HSM support. also audit log retention and KMS key rotation policy.
[03:31] Marcus Lee: we support customer-managed KMS in Private deploys and rotation policies; for hosted we have an optional bring-your-own-key integration for enterprise plans. we'll include the SOC2 and encryption docs.
[03:41] Aisha Khan: perfect. procurement will ask for SOC2/ISO attestation, and possibly a network diagram.
[03:46] Priya Patel: we'll attach the security pack to the follow-up email.
[03:50] Tom Reynolds: about pilot scope — we want to test two models: a smaller open model for chat-like patient intake flows and a reranker/embedding flow for analytics queries. can we pin model versions?
[04:03] Sofia Ramos: yes model pinning is supported; for the pilot we recommend two endpoints: "intake-chat-v1" with latency target 120-200ms p95 and "analytics-embed-v1" with higher throughput and batched embeddings. we'll define batch sizes and GPU types in the pilot config.
[04:21] Ben Park: what's realistic for token-based cost during pilot? we have budget constraints — we can't blow the monthly budget.
[04:29] Priya Patel: we'll provide a pilot pricing estimate: usually we set a capped spend for the two-week pilot. Redwood Optimize can help tune batch/caching to lower token unit costs.
[04:39] Maya Singh: if we run pilot in Private on our VPC, does the billing still go through Redwood? we need invoice paths for procurement.
[04:47] Marcus Lee: billing options include centralized billing to your procurement or self-bill via invoice; we'll coordinate with your finance team.
[04:53] Aisha Khan: success criteria — what should we measure?
[04:57] Sofia Ramos: propose top-level metrics: p95 latency, tokens/sec, correctness/quality on the curated prompt set (measured by precision/recall or human eval), and cost per 1k tokens. also availability and error rates.
[05:12] Ben Park: we'll create a 50-sample prompt set, plus 10 edge cases with PHI-ish structure (anonymized) to stress test conversation contexts.
[05:21] Tom Reynolds: for monitoring, we want token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards — can Redwood expose Prometheus metrics or do you integrate with Datadog?
[05:30] Sofia Ramos: we have integrations for Datadog and can expose traces; we'll provide a sample dashboard template and webhook for alerts.
[05:39] Maya Singh: about compliance — the legal team will request a Data Processing Addendum and SCAs. can you share standard DPA and security questionnaires?
[05:47] Priya Patel: yes, we'll attach DPA, subprocessor list, penetration test summary, and the SOC2 report. Expect that in the follow-up email.
[05:54] Marcus Lee: let's recap next steps: Priya will send onboarding materials; Tom will share VPC diagram; Sofia and Ben to draft pilot config; Maya to confirm KMS; Marcus to schedule pilot planning.
[06:08] Aisha Khan: timeline-wise we want pilot setup that week (Jan 27) and initial perf results two weeks after.
[06:15] Priya Patel: sounds good. any final concerns or blockers?
[06:20] Tom Reynolds: just internal procurement review timelines — i'll flag any delays.
[06:24] Maya Singh: i'll need to see KMS docs to sign off.
[06:28] Priya Patel: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the deck + security pack and proposed pilot dates.
[06:33] Ben Park: thanks, bye.
[06:35] Aisha Khan: appreciate it, bye.
